subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: After a deferred maintenance timeout releases a session lane, should OpenClaw permit the timed-out plugin `maintain()` invocation to continue while later maintenance may be scheduled, relying on the new core-side fence for transcript and task mutations?
rationale: The patch safely blocks several core-owned late side effects, but it cannot cancel or fully constrain plugin-owned work. Choosing whether continued plugin execution and later maintenance overlap are acceptable defines the runtime contract rather than a mechanical implementation detail.

options.title: Adopt the opt-in fence contract
options.body: Accept continued plugin execution after the lane timeout, document that only core-owned late mutations are fenced, and merge after a fresh rebase and required checks.

options.title: Require stronger lifecycle ownership
options.body: Rework the design so timed-out maintenance remains coalesced or is otherwise prevented from overlapping with a subsequent same-session maintenance run before landing.

options.title: Use an existing timeout policy instead
options.body: Decline the new configuration key and route deferred maintenance through an already-approved host safety-timeout contract with explicit plugin semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt the opt-in fence contract
recommendation.body: Accept continued plugin execution after the lane timeout, document that only core-owned late mutations are fenced, and merge after a fresh rebase and required checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The current contributor has the most direct implementation context in the supplied history, although a repository owner should make the product-contract decision.
